headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and broad egress create dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict pathways between Claude Code and LightAgent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files, use MCP, and runs with stdin/stdout; LightAgent uses MCP over stdio/SSE and runtime hooks can observe/replace lifecycle payloads. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path where one agent’s outputs can be parsed as instructions by the other. The pairwise interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF both agents exchange content through a shared MCP server or stdio bridge, injected instructions can traverse between them.
IF either agent treats file or tool output as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents.
Route inter-agent messages through a sanitizer that strips instructions.
Use separate workspaces and separate terminals for each agent.
Require human review before either agent executes tool-derived directives.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while LightAgent handles conversations, memory, trace data, tool results, and workflow state. Both have broad network egress and MCP access, so sensitive workspace data can flow from A into B’s outputs or external APIs. The shared-workspace risk is explicit for A and B’s data handling is broad, making leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, A’s code and git history can be exposed to B.
IF B forwards tool results or memory to external APIs, data from A can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Remove secrets from the shared cwd before running either agent.
Disable network egress for one agent during joint tasks.
Review B’s memory and trace retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can modify filesystem and git state, and LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use MCP; both support multiple instances. Because both can mutate shared resources without any documented locking between them, concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The profiles directly show overlapping write surfaces, so this is a strong pairwise conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF both agents modify git state in the same repo without locks, commits and working-tree changes can conflict.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Serialize git operations with a human gate.
Use read-only mounts for one agent during the other’s write phase.
Run one agent at a time for shared repos.
requires-engineering: add file- and git-locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, shell actions, and repo changes, while LightAgent consumes tool results, workflow state, and provenance metadata. That makes it plausible for B to treat A’s output as authoritative and propagate mistakes into downstream actions. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, so this is medium rather than high, but the interaction exists in default agent workflows.
conditions: IF B uses A’s generated text or code as an input artifact without verification, errors can cascade.
IF A produces incorrect facts or commands that B then executes, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B acts on A’s output.
Require tests or linting before any commit from A is accepted.
Limit B to summarization rather than execution for A-derived content.
Have a human approve high-impact actions.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and shell environment data, while LightAgent handles API keys and long-term memory/trace data. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be proven; however, the pair clearly moves sensitive operational data across two different retention surfaces. Uncertainty prevents a lower rating because the data classes are broad and undocumented.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the workspace, both agents may process it under different retention/logging regimes.
IF either agent stores traces or memory longer than the other, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace.
Check both agents’ retention settings before use.
Disable memory or trace persistence where possible.
Keep secrets in external vaults, not in files.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both agents.
